  "question": "What has been proposed to reduce the risk of people wrongly assuming that an autonomous car will repeat a familiar maneuver when traffic conditions call for a different one, and by what mechanism?",
  "reference_answer": "The proposal is coverage-augmented algorithmic teaching: deliberately showing users informative examples of the car’s behavior, selected using a model of how people infer its objectives. The best-performing version uses a deterministic, Euclidean-based approximate-inference model. First, the algorithm selects examples predicted to increase the user’s belief in the car’s actual objective. Once additional examples offer little improvement under that model, it adds informative examples covering the remaining maneuver strategies. This addresses an observed failure: seeing one strategy without its alternative can make users expect that strategy in every situation of that type. Showing, for example, both merging ahead and braking to merge behind helps users understand that the car’s choices depend on its objectives and the circumstances, rather than on a fixed maneuver rule. That richer understanding is intended to improve predictions in unfamiliar situations. In the reported study, the combined approach significantly outperformed a random-example baseline.",
  "spans": [
    "In other words, if users see one trajectory strategy in the training examples and not the opposite strategy, they tend to think the autonomous car will always take the first strategy in that environment type.",
    "we model how humans make inferences about the robot’s objective function from examples of its optimal behavior, to generate examples that increase the probability of the correct inferred objective function.",
    "The best approximate-inference model used the Euclidean-based distance with deterministic effects.",
    "so that first the examples that maximize the probability of θ∗ will\nbe selected, and only after no further examples will significantly\nimprove the probability of θ∗, extra examples are selected to\nprovide coverage across the strategies.\nWe select these extra examples by choosing the best with\nrespect to the approximate-inference model M, to make sure they are informative.",
    "The insight underlying our approach is that the key to end-users being able to anticipate what a robot will do in novel situations is having a good mental model or understanding of the robot’s objective function.",
    "The coverage augmentation enabled it to significantly outperform the random baseline (with a Welch’s t-test p=0.049), which suggests coverage is useful."
  ]
